summary: ```# Marvelous Designer 2025.0: [Beta] Fur Strand in 3D Window Welcome to the Marvelous Designer 2025.0 version new feature videos. In the 2025 version, the **fur strand** type has been added to the material of fabric. ## Overview of Fur Strand Fur strands can be used not only for fabric but also for piping and binding using fabric. Fur strands are displayed both in the 3D window and in the Quality render. They can be exported in USD format, allowing us to edit in other 3D software. To export strand data with the USD, select **Include Fur Strand Data**. ## Accessing Fur Strand Features Let's take a look at the fur strand features. The menu for fur strand can be found in three different locations: 1. **Fabric Properties**: Set the material type to fur strand, then configure the fur preset and child properties. The shape of the fur strand can be set here. 2. **Main Menu Settings**: Go to **Preferences > 3D Fur Strand Shape**. You can choose from three options: - **Cylinder**: Displays fur in a cylindrical shape with thickness and width, useful for checking the full structure of the fur strand. - **Plane**: Displays fur in a planar shape without thickness but with width. - **Line**: Displays fur in spline curves without thickness or width. Please note that simulation speed may be significantly slower when the fur strand display is enabled, as it requires additional calculations in the 3D window. To improve performance, you can disable *Show Fur Strand* in the garment rendering options under the 3D display icons. It is recommended to enable this option only when necessary. If you want to see each fur strand in a random color, please turn on **Random Fur Strand Color**. Additionally, when recording or playing animations, it is advisable to turn off *Show Fur Strand*, as simulation speed may decrease if it is enabled. ## Applying Fur Strand to Fabric To apply fur strand to the fabric, follow these steps: 1. In the **Object Browser**, select the fabric to which you want to apply the fur strand. 2. In the **Property Editor**, set the material type to fur strand. Once selected, the fur strand will be displayed in the 3D window, and the fur strand properties will appear in the property editor. 3. You can also select a fur preset in advance, which includes multiple predefined fur shapes. ## Fur Parameters ### Melanin - Configures the saturation of the fur's original color. A higher melanin value results in a more saturated color, while a lower value produces a lighter color. ### Pheomelanin - Configures how reddish the fur is. A higher pheomelanin value means redder fur. The pheomelanin value is applied in proportion to the melanin value and is not counted when the melanin value is zero. ### Glossiness - Configures the shininess of the fur. Higher values result in shinier fur, especially when light is applied. ### Softness - Expresses the smoothness of the fur. A higher softness value makes the fur smoother, while a lower value makes it rougher. ### Fur Gradation Color - This feature allows you to apply gradient color to the middle and end of the fur. When enabled, related menus will appear at the bottom. - **Mid Color**: The middle color of the fur. - **Tip Color**: The end color of the fur. You can adjust the scaling of the gradient area by modifying the mid position (start position of the middle color) and the tip position (start position of the end color). When interpolation is enabled, the boundaries between the root, middle, and tip colors will blend smoothly for a more natural appearance. ## Fur Shape Preferences The fur shape preferences allow you to define the detailed shape of the fur: ### Base Properties - **Length**: Controls the length of the fur. A higher value means longer fur. - **Thickness**: Configures the thickness of a single thread of fur. A higher value results in thicker fur. - **Bend**: Configures the bending strength of the fur. A higher value means the fur is more affected by gravity and bends more. - **Taper**: Differentiates the thickness of the fur between its root and end. A higher value results in thinner fur toward the end. - **Density**: Configures how closely fur strands are placed. Higher values mean denser fur. - **Segments**: Configures how many sections a single thread of fur is divided into. For long and higher-bending fur, a higher segment value is needed for smooth and realistic bending. You can use base maps to express different lengths, thicknesses, and densities within a single pattern. The value of zero is multiplied to the length, thickness, and density when a map is black, while a value of one is multiplied when a map is white. ### Fur Cluster Generator To create a realistic fur cluster, click on the **Cluster of Fur Shape** in the fur properties. The fur cluster generator window will appear, allowing you to create a realistic fur cluster using the length map (adjusting length) and the bend direction map (controlling bend direction). #### Adjusting the Length Map - You can adjust the cropping map to apply different fur lengths within a single pattern. If you are not using a separate cropping map, the detail options will be disabled. - To load images for texture map uses, click on the crop option. Once images are loaded, they will be merged into the basic grayscale maps, and other preferences will be activated. The cropping map is a grayscale-based image, where brightness or transparency represents fur length. Translucent and black areas represent the shortest length, while opaque and white areas represent the longest length. ## Additional Parameters ### Bending Intensity - Adjust the bending intensity of the fur's direction using the intensity value in the cluster submenu. This strengthens the fur clumps, giving them a more pronounced three-dimensional appearance. ### Pore Density - Adjusts the density of the fur cluster. Higher values create smaller and denser clumps, while lower values result in larger, wider clumps. ### Direction Intensity Random Function - Controls whether the fur's bend direction remains consistent or becomes more irregular. ### Detail Cluster Menu - Adjust the aggregation strength of the detail clusters while maintaining the fur's bending preferences from the available options. A higher relax value can soften the boundaries of the fur clumps, giving them a smoother appearance. ## Gravity and Curl Parameters ### Gravity - Adjust the strength of gravity using Vector X, Y, and Z to manually set the gravity value along each axis. ### Curl - **Radius**: Controls the curl radius of the fur. Higher values result in greater twisting, while lower values make the fur thinner and less twisted. - **Number**: Controls the number of waves in the fur. Higher values create more twisted fur, while lower values result in less twisted fur. ### Variance - **Length**: Can be expressed irregularly or uniformly. Higher values create more irregular lengths, while lower values yield uniform lengths. - **Thickness**: Can also be expressed irregularly or uniformly. - **Direction**: The bend direction of the fur can be expressed in similar ways. - **Gravity**: The gravity applied to the fur can be expressed irregularly or uniformly, requiring a bend value greater than zero to take effect. ### Randomization Seed - You can use the parameters of the same fur to achieve random results. ```
